archetype.name: Point Guard (Shanahan distributor)
archetype.definition: A rhythm passer who wins by putting the ball on time to whoever the play design frees, with layups under center and in the middle of the field, plus enough scrambling to punish broken plays.

report.headline: Elite efficiency built on weak defenses and Mike Evans, now without both
report.take:
Purdy is what he has been since 2023: an accurate, on-schedule distributor in Kyle Shanahan's offense whose efficiency regularly ranks with the league's best. His 0.348 EPA per dropback ranks 4th of 45 and his 6.18 CPOE 5th, close to his 2023 (5.38) and 2025 (7.23) accuracy. The 49ers lead the league in pass EPA and success rate. He isn't a creator who carries an offense. He is a very good operator of one, and the system feeds him: under center he completes 76.8% with a 14.9 CPOE, and throws to the middle return 0.651 EPA a play.

The headline numbers rest on two pillars, and both are shakier than the season line suggests. The first is the schedule. His two monster games, 23.3 and 22.9 passing EPA, came against Miami and Arizona, now ranked 29th and 28th in defense. In the last three weeks, against Denver (7th), Seattle (2nd) and Washington, his EPA per dropback fell to 0.109 and his sack rate nearly doubled to 5.4%. Seattle pressured him on 35.3% of dropbacks and held him to negative EPA. The second pillar is Mike Evans: 40 targets at 1.023 EPA each, by far the biggest source of value in the passing game. Kittle is useful at 0.372 a target, while McCaffrey's 35 targets have lost value.

Some of the shine will wear off. Ten red-zone touchdowns on 34 attempts with a 16.6 CPOE is a hot streak. The 8.2% TD rate (3rd) and the 40-TD pace should cool toward his career norm. His interceptions should rise too: he threw 11, 12 and 10 in his last three seasons, the 10 in only nine games, but has just 2 this year. His bad-throw rate (11.7%) is unchanged from last year, so the turnover drop is more luck than a new skill. What does look real is his sack avoidance. His pressure-to-sack rate has gone from about 30% in 2023-24 to 16.7% last year to 10.7% now, ranked 1st. A slightly longer time to throw paired with 0.909 EPA per scramble and 9 scramble first downs makes that a trade that pays.

The near future depends on who is catching the ball. Deebo Samuel is out until roughly November 8, Christian Kirk is on IR, and Evans is listed doubtful with Achilles soreness. That leaves a passing game funneled through Kittle, McCaffrey and Juszczyk, which favors volume of short completions over the explosive value that made his season. Expect a capable, efficient starter rather than an MVP-pace one until the receivers return.

strengths.title: Scheme-fed accuracy in the middle
strengths.body: His best work comes where Shanahan's design does the most for him: under center, off play-action, and between the numbers. He has been an accuracy-over-expected passer in three of his four seasons, so this is his identity, not a blip. It should hold as long as the scheme is intact, though the explosive value it produces depends on who runs the routes.

strengths.title: Sacks avoided, scrambles converted
strengths.body: He rarely turns pressure into sacks, ranking 1st in both sack rate and pressure-to-sack rate. His scrambles are a real weapon at 0.909 EPA apiece. This is a two-year trend after middling rates in 2023-24, so it looks like real growth in how he handles the pocket. Even so, Seattle showed it can break when the pressure rate climbs past a third of dropbacks.

strengths.title: Efficient past ten air yards
strengths.body: Throws of 10+ air yards return 0.606 EPA a play. The intermediate level (0.518) carries a real sample of 48 attempts, and deep shots have hit too. The deep number rests on only 16 attempts and leans heavily on Evans, so treat the intermediate level as the durable part.

concerns.title: Receiver room is being gutted
concerns.body: Evans has been the engine of this passing game, Deebo is out into November, and Kirk is on IR. Without them, targets shift toward McCaffrey, whose targets have actually cost EPA. That trims the explosive plays the season was built on. It is a temporary but real hit to his ceiling.

concerns.title: Touchdowns and turnovers due to normalize
concerns.body: Ten red-zone TDs with a 16.6 CPOE there, and only 2 interceptions, are both running hotter than his history. He threw double-digit picks in each of the last three seasons, and his bad-throw rate hasn't improved. Expect fewer touchdowns and a few more interceptions from here.

concerns.title: Softer against real defenses
concerns.body: His last three games against stronger opponents show a far more ordinary passer. His EPA per dropback was down by nearly a quarter-point and his sack rate was up, with Seattle's pressure exposing him most. Part of that is schedule, but it shows the season line is flattered by Miami and Arizona.

trend.note: After a blistering Weeks 2-3 against bottom-five defenses, his per-play value has sagged against Denver and Seattle, and stayed modest against a weak Washington unit with Deebo inactive. The 5-0 record over the last five hides a passer drifting from spectacular to merely good.

nextGame.headline: Thin Falcons secondary meets a depleted 49ers receiver room
nextGame.body:
Atlanta's defense is average against the pass (15th in pass EPA) but generous to quarterbacks by volume: it allows 273.2 yards a game to the position, ranked 25th. It also takes away the deep ball (4th in deep EPA) and hits quarterbacks often (6th in hit rate) without finishing sacks (20th in sack rate). That profile suits Purdy's game: short and intermediate timing throws, sack avoidance and scrambles, rather than a shot-heavy plan. Opponents pass against Atlanta more than usual (4th-strongest pass funnel), and Falcons opponents' backs see an above-normal share of targets, which fits San Francisco's RB- and TE-heavy look without its receivers. The Book has SF -3.5 with a 49.5 total.

Availability cuts both ways. Atlanta's secondary is thin: CB C.J. Henderson is out, CB Billy Bowman Jr. is questionable with a hamstring, and linebackers Divine Deablo (arm) and Kendal Daniels (neck) are both questionable after leaving their last game. That opens the middle of the field, where Purdy is at his best. On his side, Evans is doubtful, and Deebo and Kirk are out, so the targets that produced most of his explosive value may not be on the field. Kittle, McCaffrey and Juszczyk become the passing game.

keyMatchups.title: Kittle and backs versus depleted linebackers
keyMatchups.body: With two Falcons linebackers questionable after injuries, the seams and flats Kittle and McCaffrey work should be softer. Atlanta lets top tight ends and lead backs score above their averages. This is the most likely path to efficiency without Evans.

keyMatchups.title: Deep shots into a stingy deep defense
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta ranks 4th in deep EPA allowed. Purdy's big deep numbers come on just 16 attempts, mostly with Evans. Expect a capped explosive-play ceiling unless Evans plays.

keyMatchups.title: Hits without sacks
keyMatchups.body: Atlanta gets to quarterbacks often but converts few into sacks, which matches Purdy's 1st-ranked pressure-to-sack rate. If he keeps escaping, scrambles can add value as they have all year.

nextGame.watch: Whether Evans is active. Without him, watch how much of the explosive passing value survives in throws to Kittle and the backs.

restOfSeason.body:
The floor is sturdy. His accuracy, sack avoidance and scheme fit have held across seasons, and the 49ers' offense ranks near the top of the league. The ceiling of the first six weeks will not last. The red-zone touchdown rate and the low interception count both point toward his career norms. Over the next two or three weeks the receiver injuries also lower the explosive-play rate that powered his EPA. Once Deebo returns around November 8 and Evans is healthy, a strong-efficiency, roughly two-touchdown-a-game passer is a fair expectation.

I'd project 225-265 passing yards a game, 1.5-2.1 passing TDs, 15-28 rushing yards, and 5-9 passing EPA a game. That is still a top-10 level of efficiency, but closer to his 2025 than to his Week 2-3 peak.
swingFactors: Interception rate reverting to career norms

confidence.note: Six games with a strong multi-year track record, but heavy receiver injuries and schedule-inflated early games blur the near term.
